questions.q: In this lab, what are the three pieces that together make up the complete integration?
options: A Scripted REST API, a Business Rule, and a Scheduled Job
A REST Message, a Function, and a Script Include method
An Authentication Profile, a MID Server, and a Spoke
A Table API record and two ACLs
questions.explain: The lab assembles exactly what Lessons 4-6 covered: one REST Message (the connection), one Function (the operation), and one Script Include method (the calling code).

questions.q: Why does the Script Include check httpStatus != 200 before calling JSON.parse() on the response body?
options: JSON.parse() cannot run inside a try/catch block
ServiceNow requires a status check before every script statement
A non-200 response body isn't guaranteed to be valid JSON, so parsing it directly could throw a separate, confusing error
httpStatus has no relationship to the response body's content
questions.explain: Checking the status first lets the method return a clear error message for an HTTP-level failure, rather than risking a JSON parsing exception on a body that may just be a plain-text error message.

options: ServiceNow technically forbids returning raw HTTP objects from a Script Include
The method deliberately returns a narrow shape with only the fields the caller needs, so callers never have to parse HTTP details themselves
RESTMessageV2 does not expose a getBody() method
Including the raw response would exceed a hard field-count limit
questions.explain: This is a design choice covered in the lab: callers like a Business Rule or Service Portal widget get exactly the fields they need, or a clear error, never raw HTTP or JSON details.

questions.q: The try/catch block in this lab's Script Include method covers two distinct kinds of failure. What are they?
options: A failed ACL check and a missing table column
A network-level failure thrown by execute() itself, and a parsing failure thrown by JSON.parse() if the body is malformed despite a 200 status
Only syntax errors in the Script Include's own code
A duplicate REST Message name and a duplicate Function name
questions.explain: One try/catch block covers both: execute() can throw on a true network failure (Lesson 6), and JSON.parse() can throw separately if the body isn't valid JSON even when the HTTP call itself succeeded.

questions.q: Before Step 3 (writing the Script Include) ever begins, what already happened in Steps 1-2, and why does that order matter?
options: Nothing — the Script Include is always written first in a real build
The REST Message and Function were configured and tested with a real HTTP call, isolating configuration correctness from the script that's about to be written
The Authentication Profile was deleted to simplify the lab
A Scripted REST API was built to receive the weather data
questions.explain: Following Lesson 5's discipline, the Function was tested directly from the record first; a clean 200 there means any later script issue is known to be script-side, not configuration.
